title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% Wednesday but Chair Warsh signaled a December hike is likely; Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of hiking now. Treasury yields fell after the presser; S&P 500 and Nasdaq each rose ~0.3%, Dow +0.2%.
Markets: Brent crude jumped 1.3% to top $115/bbl after Houthi militants said they targeted Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, adding to uncertainty from Israel's inconclusive election.

Companies: AI-infrastructure rally extended — Vertiv (+17%) and Flex (+12%) soared on blowout earnings and raised outlooks; Oracle (+11%) rose after capping capex at $20B through FY2030 and targeting free-cash-flow positive by H2 FY2028.

Companies: Trian Fund Management (Nelson Peltz) offered to buy Wendy's for ~$1.4B to take it private; shares +15%. Elite law firm Weil Gotshal & Manges told partners it plans to dissolve the 1,200-lawyer firm.

Companies: Mega-cap earnings split overnight — Alphabet jumped on cloud strength while Meta slid on a one-time tax charge and heavier spending guidance; Microsoft's reaction was more muted despite beating estimates.

Macro/Policy: Thursday brings GDP, personal income/spending and retail sales data, plus earnings from Amazon, Intel, Caterpillar, Eli Lilly, Merck, Mastercard, Shell and Gilead. Homeowners with resetting adjustable-rate mortgages face sharply higher payments as rates sit at 3-year highs.
